Consider the following two statements : Statement I : For any two non-zero complex numbers $z_1, z_2$, $\left(\left|z_1\right|+\left|z_2\right|\right)\left|\frac{z_1}{\left|z_1\right|}+\frac{z_2}{\left|z_2\right|}\right| \leq 2\left(\left|z_1\right|+\left|z_2\right|\right) \text {, and }$
Statement II : If $x, y, z$ are three distinct complex numbers and $\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}, \mathrm{c}$ are three positive real numbers such that $\frac{\mathrm{a}}{|y-z|}=\frac{\mathrm{b}}{|z-x|}=\frac{\mathrm{c}}{|x-y|}$, then $\frac{\mathrm{a}^2}{y-z}+\frac{\mathrm{b}^2}{z-x}+\frac{\mathrm{c}^2}{x-y}=1 .$
Between the above two statements,

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
